# Insulation panel reuse economics

Each van's insulation panels last roughly three years before the gel's thermal performance degrades enough to replace them, and the used panels currently go to disposal, which the finance lead flagged as a cost line worth a second look, not because it is large on its own but because disposal fees for anything containing a phase-change compound have risen twice in the past year under a new local waste rule.

A materials recycler two towns over has expressed informal interest in used panels for a different reason entirely: the same phase-change property that makes them good at buffering a delivery van's cargo hold makes them worth harvesting for a construction-insulation product they already sell, at a price that would roughly offset today's disposal fee if volume justified the pickup logistics. Nobody has run the actual numbers past a back-of-envelope stage, and the recycler's interest has not been tested against a real batch of panels yet, but it is the first line item in this room that turns a cost into a plausible small credit.
